questions.stem: Gregor Mendel presented his pea experiments to the Brno Natural History Society and later published the full paper. In which years did he present and then publish this work?

options.text: presented 1865, published 1866
presented 1866, published 1865
presented 1859, published 1860
presented 1900, published 1901

rationales.whyCorrect: Mendel presented his pea experiments to the Brno Natural History Society in 1865 and published the paper in 1866. B swaps the two years. C substitutes 1859, the year of Darwin's On the Origin of Species. questions.stem: A diploid pea plant carries two alleles at the flower color locus. According to Mendel's law of segregation, what happens to these two alleles during gamete formation?

options.text: The two alleles blend into a single mixed allele before entering a gamete
The two alleles separate so that each gamete receives exactly one of them
Alleles at different loci enter gametes independently of one another
Both alleles are packaged together into the same gamete

rationales.whyCorrect: The law of segregation states that the two alleles carried at a locus are separated during gamete formation so each gamete receives one allele, which is why a heterozygote produces the two gamete types in equal numbers. A describes blending inheritance, the idea Mendel's counts ruled out. C states the law of independent assortment, which governs alleles at different loci. D describes the opposite of segregation, with both alleles entering the same gamete.
rationales.eli10: Suppose one red marble and one blue marble must be split between two pockets. Each pocket ends with exactly one marble, never both marbles and never a mixed purple marble. That is what happens to the two versions of a gene when an organism makes eggs or sperm. The two versions separate, one into each egg or sperm, and that is the law of segregation.
rationales.distractorAnalysis: The law of segregation states that the two alleles carried at a locus are separated during gamete formation so each gamete receives one allele, which is why a heterozygote produces the two gamete types in equal numbers. A describes blending inheritance, the idea Mendel's counts ruled out. C states the law of independent assortment, which governs alleles at different loci. D describes the opposite of segregation, with both alleles entering the same gamete.

questions.stem: Mendel crossed pea plants that differed at two loci and found that the allele combinations in the offspring were shuffled freely. Which statement describes the law of independent assortment?

options.text: Alleles at different loci are transmitted to offspring independently of one another
The two alleles at a single locus separate during gamete formation
The phenotype of a heterozygote is an exact blend of the two parental phenotypes
Alleles at loci on the same chromosome are always transmitted together

rationales.whyCorrect: Independent assortment holds that alleles at different loci are distributed to gametes independently, so a dihybrid produces the four gamete classes in equal proportions. B states the law of segregation, which concerns a single locus. C is blending inheritance, which Mendel's results ruled out. D describes complete linkage, which is broken whenever crossing over separates the loci.
rationales.eli10: Think of shuffling two decks of cards side by side. The card drawn from the first deck has nothing to do with the card drawn from the second deck. That is how two genes stored on different chromosomes, the long packages of DNA in the cell, behave. Each gene is shuffled on its own, so the versions that end up together are mixed freely.
rationales.distractorAnalysis: Independent assortment holds that alleles at different loci are distributed to gametes independently, so a dihybrid produces the four gamete classes in equal proportions. B states the law of segregation, which concerns a single locus. C is blending inheritance, which Mendel's results ruled out. D describes complete linkage, which is broken whenever crossing over separates the loci.

questions.stem: In 1910, Thomas Hunt Morgan found a white eyed male fly among the red eyed Drosophila in his laboratory. What key conclusion came from this experiment?

options.text: The white eye trait is carried on the Y chromosome only
Eye color in Drosophila is inherited through the cytoplasm
The white eye allele is X linked, establishing that genes are carried on chromosomes
White eye is a dominant autosomal trait

A fails because the allele moved through daughters, who never receive a Y chromosome. B describes cytoplasmic inheritance, which would pass through the egg to all offspring. D is ruled out because the trait is recessive and appears almost exclusively in males.

That pattern was the clue that the gene sits on the X chromosome, one of the two chromosomes that decide sex. One fly experiment showed that genes really are carried on chromosomes.

questions.stem: A researcher wants to map the positions of many genes along chromosomes by counting recombinant offspring in many crosses. Which model organism is the best first choice for this work?

options.text: Escherichia coli, because its small circular chromosome is easy to transform

questions.stem: In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick proposed a structure for DNA using data that included Rosalind Franklin's X ray diffraction images. Which statement about DNA follows directly from their model?

DNA is a double helix with antiparallel strands whose base pairing suggests a copying mechanism
DNA is a triple helix held together by base stacking alone
DNA is a helical protein whose amino acid order stores the information

rationales.whyCorrect: The Watson and Crick model described DNA as a double helix in which two antiparallel strands pair A with T and G with C by hydrogen bonds, and that complementarity directly suggested how one strand could copy the other. A describes a transfer RNA like single strand. C mistakes the double helix for a triple helix. D reflects the earlier idea that protein, not DNA, was the hereditary material.

questions.stem: The Human Genome Project was an international effort to determine the sequence of human DNA. Which statement about the project is correct?

It was completed in 2001 with the sequence of the Drosophila genome

The chance that one flip lands recessive is one half, and the chance for the other flip is also one half. questions.stem: Two pea plants heterozygous for flower color with genotype *Aa* x *Aa* are crossed, with complete dominance of A over a and normal segregation at this single locus. What phenotypic ratio is expected among the offspring?

options.text: 3:1 dominant to recessive

questions.stem: The history of genetics includes the eugenics movement, which misused heredity claims to justify forced sterilization, and many modern geneticists say the field needs safeguards because of that history. Which statement best reflects the ethical debate?

The benefits of genetics are so great that the history of misuse has no relevance to current practice
Some argue that this history requires stronger oversight of genetic research, while others warn that excessive restrictions could slow beneficial research
Decisions about genetic research should be made only by government agencies, never by individual scientists

It is a mammal whose physiology closely matches human physiology

questions.stem: A cell in the G1 phase sustains DNA damage, and the DNA damage checkpoint responds by stopping the cell cycle. Which protein is responsible for this arrest?

options.text: cyclin dependent kinase 2
cyclin dependent kinase 1
retinoblastoma protein
p53 tumor suppressor

rationales.whyCorrect: The p53 tumor suppressor, encoded by *TP53*, is the effector of the DNA damage response: it triggers cell cycle arrest so the cell can repair the damage or undergo apoptosis. questions.stem: A human spermatocyte with 46 chromosomes (2n = 46) completes meiosis I without any errors. What is the chromosome content of each of the two daughter cells produced at the end of meiosis I?

options.text: 46 chromosomes, each with two sister chromatids
46 chromosomes, each with one chromatid
23 chromosomes, each with two sister chromatids
23 chromosomes, each with one chromatid

rationales.whyCorrect: Meiosis I is the reductional division: homologous chromosomes separate, so the chromosome number is cut in half, from 46 to 23 chromosomes per daughter cell. Sister chromatids remain joined through meiosis I, so each of the 23 chromosomes still carries two chromatids. Option D describes the post-meiosis II products, and options A and B keep the diploid count instead of halving it.

Each sock still has its mate attached by the cuff, like two sister chromatids. Meiosis II then splits each cuff, giving each person 23 single socks.

questions.stem: During meiosis II in a human testis, the sister chromatids of one chromosome fail to separate while all other chromosomes behave normally. If a sperm that is aneuploid as a result of this error fertilizes a normal egg, which chromosome numbers are possible in the resulting zygote?

rationales.whyCorrect: Sister chromatids separate in meiosis II, so their failure to separate sends both copies into one sperm and none into another: one sperm carries n + 1 = 24 chromosomes and one carries n - 1 = 22. Option D keeps only the 47 outcome, option A assumes the error is corrected, and option C double-counts the mis-segregated chromosome.

That bag gets an extra sock and another bag gets none, while the rest are fine. When each bag meets an ordinary bag from the other parent, the mix makes a normal total, an extra-sock total, or a missing-sock total. The mistake shows up as a count one too high or one too low, never as the correct count.

questions.stem: During mitosis, replicated chromosomes are pulled to opposite poles of the cell. Which structure of the chromosome is the site where spindle microtubules attach?

options.text: the centromere
the telomere
the origin of replication
the nucleosome

rationales.whyCorrect: The centromere is the constricted region where the sister chromatids of a replicated chromosome are held together and where the kinetochore assembles, providing the site of spindle microtubule attachment that pulls the chromosome apart. Mixing the centromere with the telomere is the classic error here.

questions.stem: A karyotype prepared from a patient's blood sample shows 47 chromosomes, including two X chromosomes and one Y chromosome. Which condition is indicated by this karyotype?

options.text: Down syndrome (trisomy 21)
Turner syndrome (45,X)
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY)
Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18)

rationales.whyCorrect: A 47,XXY karyotype is the finding in Klinefelter syndrome, a sex chromosome aneuploidy listed as an extra X chromosome. Turner syndrome has only 45 chromosomes with a single X, so it is excluded by the count.
rationales.eli10: A karyotype is like a photo lineup of all the chromosome pairs lined up by size. Most people have two photos in every pair, and either two X photos or an X and a Y photo at the end. Down syndrome and Edwards syndrome are autosome trisomies (trisomy 21 and trisomy 18) with 47 chromosomes as well, but their karyotypes show an extra autosome, not an XXY sex chromosome constitution. questions.stem: A human liver cell contains 46 chromosomes in G1. How many chromosomes does each daughter cell contain immediately after this cell completes mitosis and cytokinesis?

Option B applies meiotic halving, option C counts chromatids as chromosomes, and option D inserts a nondisjunction error that a normal mitosis does not make.

questions.stem: Each round of DNA replication shortens the ends of linear chromosomes, and the enzyme telomerase counteracts this loss in cells that need many divisions. Which molecule provides the RNA template used by telomerase to extend telomeres?

the *BRCA1* protein
the *DNMT1* protein
the *TERC* RNA component

questions.stem: The second meiotic division is described as equational. What does equational mean in this context?

options.text: homologous chromosomes segregate
sister chromatids separate so chromosome number stays constant
the DNA content is doubled before division
crossing over occurs between homologs

rationales.whyCorrect: Meiosis II is equational because the chromosome number is unchanged: sister chromatids separate, and each daughter cell keeps the same chromosome count as the cell that entered the division. questions.stem: A researcher treats a population of dividing cells with a drug that specifically inhibits cyclin dependent kinase 1, the kinase that drives entry into mitosis. In which phase of the cell cycle would the treated cells accumulate?

G1 phase
S phase

questions.stem: A researcher proposes using CRISPR-Cas9 to edit a disease-causing mutation in human embryos before implantation, so that the change would be inherited by all descendants. Which statement best captures the main ethical debate surrounding this proposal?

Germline editing raises no special concern because the edited DNA is present in only one individual

questions.stem: In a whole genome sequencing project, which step joins millions of short overlapping reads into long contiguous genomic segments, a prerequisite for any further analysis?

Annotation
Variant calling
Sequence alignment

questions.stem: When two sequences are aligned, the alignment is scored for identity and similarity. Which statement correctly distinguishes the two measures?

options.text: Identity counts every aligned position, while similarity counts only exact matches.

Identity counts only positions where the aligned residues are exactly the same, while similarity also credits positions where the residues differ but share chemical properties, such as both being hydrophobic.
Identity measures the length of the alignment, while similarity measures the fraction of matching bases.
Identity and similarity are interchangeable terms for the same alignment score.

questions.stem: A researcher has sequenced a novel human cDNA and runs a BLAST search against a database of characterized genes. The top hit is a mouse gene sharing 92% sequence identity with the query across its full length. Which conclusion is best supported by this result?

The 92% identity proves the two proteins are functionally identical in every context.
The novel gene is likely the human counterpart of the mouse gene, so it probably performs the same biochemical function.

questions.stem: A team wants to identify every genomic region where a specific transcription factor binds in a human cell line. Which approach is the most direct way to answer this question?

RNA-seq of the cell line.
ChIP-seq using an antibody against the transcription factor.
Two color microarray comparing the cell line with a reference sample.

Gene R carries a mutation in the tumor that increases its mRNA level.
Gene R's protein is ten times more abundant in the tumor than in the normal tissue.

The finding should be handled under a disclosure policy that balances the participant's autonomy, including the right not to know, against the scope of the original consent, and many research programs address such incidental findings with an opt in choice about receiving them.

questions.stem: A genome browser displays a small contig whose coding strand is 5' ATG AAG TAA GCT CGT 3', and no features are annotated yet. Which annotation of the open reading frame is correct?

questions.stem: In a large randomly mating population with no selection, mutation, migration, or drift, what does the equation p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1 describe?

The phenotypic ratio produced by a cross between two *Aa* parents

The probability that two unrelated individuals both carry allele *a*

D misreads the equation as an individual matching probability rather than a population genotype census.

questions.stem: Which condition is required for a population to remain in Hardy Weinberg equilibrium at a locus?

options.text: Individuals mate preferentially with genetically similar partners

Heterozygotes have higher fitness than either homozygote
Mating is random with respect to the locus, and selection, mutation, migration, and drift are absent
